## Introduction

This document presents the results of the impact of the adoption of cosy tariff on smart meter electricity consumption at the household level.

- Can we find out when they install their HP

- epc data



```{r download-data}
# Save results because downloading / processing is very long
if (!file.exists("data/scratch/aggregated_data.RDS")) {
  if (!file.exists("data/scratch/smart_meters.RDS")) {
    
    library(bigrquery)
    
    
    # Store the project ID
    projectid = 'cnz-data-warehouse-d66eb552a5'
    
    # Set your query
    sql = 'SELECT mpan, interval_start, consumption_kwh FROM `cnz-data-warehouse-d66eb552a5.src_cosy.heatpump`'
    
    # Run the query; this returns a bq_table object that you can query further
    tb <- bq_project_query(projectid, sql)
    
    # Store the data in a tibble
    consumption_data <-bq_table_download(tb, n_max=Inf, bigint="integer64", page=250000)
    unique_consumption_data <- unique(consumption_data, by = c("mpan", "datetime"))
    
    # Save
    saveRDS(unique_consumption_data, "data/scratch/smart_meters.RDS")
    
  } else {
    consumption_data <- readRDS("data/scratch/smart_meters.RDS")
  }
  
  
  # load agreement data to know when they switched to cosy
  # this part could be improved by adding which tariff they are on 
  # I have been ignoring that people can switch back to non cosy
  
  agreement_data <- fread("data/input/Cosy agreement.csv")%>%
    mutate(mpan = as.character(mpan)) %>%
    filter(product_display_name=="Cosy Octopus") %>%
    group_by(mpan) %>%
    arrange(agreement_valid_from) %>%
    slice(1)
  
  # create dummy for cosy adoption
  consumption_data <- consumption_data %>%
    left_join(agreement_data %>% select(mpan, agreement_valid_from, tariff_gsp_group_id, tariff_gsp_group_name), by="mpan")  %>%
    mutate(date = as.Date(datetime),
           agreement_valid_from = as.Date(agreement_valid_from),
           is_on_cosy = ifelse(date>= agreement_valid_from,1, 0),
           is_on_cosy = ifelse(is.na(is_on_cosy), 0, is_on_cosy),
           weeks_since_cosy = ifelse(!is.na(agreement_valid_from), 
                                     floor(as.numeric(difftime(datetime, agreement_valid_from, units = "weeks"))), 
                                     NA),
           hour = hour(datetime),
           rate_period = case_when(
             hour >= 4 & hour < 7   ~ "Morning Cosy",
             hour >= 13 & hour < 16 ~ "Afternoon Cosy",
             hour >= 16 & hour < 19 ~ "Peak Rate",
             TRUE                   ~ "Other"
           ))
  
  saveRDS(consumption_data, "data/scratch/smart_meters_merged.RDS")
  
  # Aggregate the data
  aggregated_data <- consumption_data %>%
    group_by(mpan, tariff_gsp_group_id, tariff_gsp_group_name, rate_period,is_on_cosy, date, weeks_since_cosy) %>%
    summarise(total_consumption = sum(consumption_kwh)) 
  
  rm(consumption_data)
  saveRDS(aggregated_data, "data/scratch/aggregated_data.RDS")
} else {
  aggregated_data <- readRDS("data/scratch/aggregated_data.RDS")
}

```

## Difference in differences

We run the following model by period and on total daily consumption for all customers that have adopted Cosy in the past year: 

$$Consumption_{it} = \alpha OnCosy_{it} + \delta_t +  \gamma_i + GSP \times \delta_t+  \epsilon_{it} $$
with:
- $Consumption_{it}$ - electricty consumption in kWh (column 1) and log (column 2) for customer $i$ on day $t$ 
- $OnCosy_{it}$ a dummy variable equals 1 if the customer has switched to Cosy, 0 otherwise. To be noted: right now, adoption is permanent, I am not switching back to 0 for people that switched to another tariff
-  $\delta_t$, $\gamma_i$, $ GSP \times \delta_t$ are day $t$,  customer $i$, and GSP regions times day fixed effects
The standard errors are clustered at the customer (MPAN) level. 

### Consumption by period

```{r, did-period, include=TRUE}


aggregated_data <- aggregated_data %>%
  left_join(weather, by=c("date"="next_date_day", "tariff_gsp_group_id" = "gsp_group_id")) %>%
    mutate(month = floor_date(date, "month")) %>%
  filter(month %in% heating_months$month)


if (!file.exists("data/scratch/did_table.RDS")) {
  
  m1 <- feols(total_consumption ~ as.factor(is_on_cosy) | date + mpan + date^tariff_gsp_group_id, 
              data = aggregated_data, 
              cluster = ~mpan, 
              split = ~ rate_period)
  
  m2 <- feols(log(total_consumption) ~ as.factor(is_on_cosy) | date + mpan + date^tariff_gsp_group_id, 
              data = aggregated_data, 
              cluster = ~mpan, 
              split = ~ rate_period)
  did_table <- etable(m1, m2)
  saveRDS(did_table, "data/scratch/did_table.RDS")
} else {
  did_table <- readRDS("data/scratch/did_table.RDS")
}

did_table
rm(did_table)


```

} else {

}
did_daily_table

## Event study

We run the following model by period for all customers that have adopted Cosy in the past year: 

$$Consumption_{it} = \sum^W _{w={-140, -9, ..., 1, ..,28}} \alpha_w WeeksSinceCosy^w_{it} + X\beta + \delta_t +  \gamma_i +  \epsilon_{it} $$
where:
- $WeeksSinceCosy^w_{it}$  is a categorical variable equals to the number of weeks before and after the adoption of Cosy. We use the week prior adoption as omitted category. 

### Consumption by period

```{r, event-study-period, eval=FALSE}

if (!file.exists("data/scratch/est_did.RDS")) {
  # Fixed-effects regression
  est_did <- feols(total_consumption ~ + i(weeks_since_cosy, -1) | date + mpan, 
                   data = aggregated_data %>% ,
                   split =~ rate_period,
                   cluster = ~mpan)
  saveRDS(est_did, "data/scratch/est_did.RDS")
} else {
  est_did <- readRDS("data/scratch/est_did.RDS")
}

# Now we can plot the result of the interaction with coefplot

coefplot(est_did[2], title="Effect on total consumption - Morning Off Peak Cosy")
coefplot(est_did[1], title="Effect on total consumption - Afternoon Off Peak Cosy")
coefplot(est_did[3], title="Effect on total consumption - Peak rate")
coefplot(est_did[4], title="Effect on total consumption - Other rate")



etable(est_did$`sample.var: rate_period; sample: Afternoon Cosy`)
etable(est_did$`sample.var: rate_period; sample: Morning Cosy`)
etable(est_did$`sample.var: rate_period; sample: Other`)
etable(est_did$`sample.var: rate_period; sample: Peak Rate`)

```

## Callaway Sant'Anna DiD

```{r, callsanta, include=TRUE}


# Getting unique rate periods to loop over
unique_periods <- unique(aggregated_data$rate_period)

if (!file.exists("data/scratch/estimates_list.RDS")) { 
  
  # Initialize a list to store estimates for each period
  estimates_list <- list()
  
  for(period in unique_periods) {
    did_data <- aggregated_data %>%
      filter(rate_period == period) %>%
      mutate(week_cosy = as.numeric(ifelse(is_on_cosy == 1, week(date), NA))) %>%
      filter(!is.na(week_cosy)) %>%
      group_by(mpan, rate_period) %>%
      summarise(firstweek = min(week_cosy, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
      inner_join(aggregated_data, by = c("mpan", "rate_period")) %>%
      mutate(week = week(date)) %>%
      group_by(mpan, firstweek, week, tariff_gsp_group_id) %>%
      summarise(total_consumption = sum(total_consumption),
                weekly_avg_cloud_cover_total = mean(daily_avg_cloud_cover_total),
                weekly_avg_heating_degree = mean(daily_avg_heating_degree),
                weekly_avg_wind_speed = mean(daily_avg_wind_speed)
      ) %>%
      mutate(id = as.numeric(mpan),
             week = as.numeric(week))
    
    # Estimating the treatment effect using the Callaway and Sant'Anna method
    est_cs <- att_gt(yname = "total_consumption",
                     tname = "week",
                     idname = "id",
                     gname = "firstweek",
                     data = did_data,
                     control_group="notyettreated",
                     allow_unbalanced_panel = TRUE)
    
    # agg
    agg.simple <- aggte(est_cs, type = "simple", na.rm = TRUE, clustervars="id")
    print(paste("Aggregate effect for", period))
    print(summary(agg.simple))
    
    # event study style
    agg.es <- aggte(est_cs, type = "dynamic", na.rm = TRUE, clustervars="id")
    
    # Store estimates in the list with period as the name
    estimates_list[[period]] <- list(simple = agg.simple, dynamic = agg.es)
    
    saveRDS(estimates_list, "data/scratch/estimates_list.RDS")
  }
} else {
  estimates_list <- readRDS("data/scratch/estimates_list.RDS")
}

for(period in unique_periods) {
  
  print(paste("Aggregate effect for", period))
  print(summary(estimates_list[[period]]$simple))
  
  # Plotting for each period
  ggdid_title <- paste(period, "Effect")
  print(ggdid(estimates_list[[period]]$dynamic, title = ggdid_title))
  
}
```
